intro: The following analysis summarizes candidate feedback for the SSC CGL 2026 Tier 1 exam held on 11 October 2026. Shift 1 has a partial overview, while Shifts 2 and 3 are still pending further reviews. All figures presented are unofficial; the SSC normalises scores across shifts for final ranking.

faqs.q: What overall difficulty was reported for the 11 October 2026 SSC CGL Tier 1 Shift 1?
faqs.a: Shift 1 on 11 October 2026 was reported as moderate overall, with each section described as moderate in difficulty.

faqs.q: How many questions were candidates able to attempt successfully in the 11 October 2026 Shift 1?
faqs.a: Candidates indicated they could attempt about 17 to 18 questions well out of the 25 presented in Shift 1.

faqs.q: Why is there no usable analysis published yet for the 11 October 2026 Shift 2 and Shift 3?
faqs.a: Both Shift 2 and Shift 3 are still pending because sufficient candidate reviews have not been collected; more evidence is needed before a reliable analysis can be released.

faqs.q: Are the figures given for the 11 October 2026 Shift 1 official SSC scores?
faqs.a: No. The numbers are unofficial estimates based on candidate feedback; the SSC will later normalise scores across all shifts for the official ranking.

faqs.q: How does the SSC normalise scores across different shifts for the 11 October 2026 exam?
faqs.a: The SSC applies a standardisation process that adjusts raw scores from each shift to a common scale, ensuring fair comparison regardless of shift difficulty variations.
